question.text: An exporter shorts 150 lots of USDINR futures at 84.50 to hedge USD 150,000 receivable. At expiry, spot is 83.00. What is the effective rate realized?

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures gain = (84.50 - 83.00) x 1000 x 150 = Rs. 2,25,000. Spot conversion of the receivable: 150,000 x 83.00 = Rs. 1,24,50,000. Total INR = Rs. 1,26,75,000, so effective rate = 1,26,75,000 / 150,000 = Rs. 84.50 per USD. Daily/final settlement of futures profit/loss supports this mechanic (p. 167). The Trap: The hedge locks in approximately the futures entry rate; spot movement alone is not the realized rate. Note: The Rs. 1.50 by which spot fell below the entry rate is exactly compensated by the futures profit, consistent with exporter hedging and effective-rate computation (pp. 97-98).
